items.title: Expose iteration as work item flag in CLI
items.body:
### Problem to solve

As a user planning work from the terminal, I want to set a work item's iteration with `glab work-items`, so I can create and schedule work without going to the UI or writing GraphQL.

Right now neither `glab work-items create` nor `glab work-items update` has an iteration flag. `glab issue create` and `glab issue update` don't have one either. The only `--iteration` flag is on `glab issue list`, where it filters results.

### Proposal

Add an `--iteration` flag to both commands:

- `glab work-items create --iteration <id>`
- `glab work-items update <iid> --iteration <id>`

`client-go` already supports this. `CreateWorkItemOptions` and `UpdateWorkItemOptions` both have an `IterationID *int64` field, sent as the GraphQL `iterationWidget`. The v3.23.0 release that glab currently pins includes it, so no dependency bump is needed. The commands only have to pass the flag value through.

### Further details

- Accepting the numeric ID is enough to start, and `glab iteration list -F json` shows the IDs. Unlike `--milestone`, looking iterations up by title isn't reliable, because iterations from automatic cadences have no title.
- Iterations are a Premium feature, so the flag only does something on instances where they are available.

### Links / references

- `client-go` `CreateWorkItemOptions.IterationID`: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/blob/main/workitems.go#L977
- `client-go` `UpdateWorkItemOptions.IterationID`: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/blob/main/workitems.go#L1357
- GraphQL `WorkItemWidgetIterationInput`: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/graphql/reference/#workitemwidgetiterationinput
